biological.citation: Heterozygous RAB3A variants cause cerebellar ataxia by a partial loss-of-function mechanism (PMID: 40166812)
biological.summary: RAB3A encodes a small GTP-binding protein abundant in brain synaptic vesicles, crucial for neurotransmitter release and synaptic plasticity. Heterozygous variants, including the recurrent p.Arg83Trp, cause autosomal dominant cerebellar ataxia; variants in the GAP-binding domain reduce GAP-dependent GTP hydrolysis. Co-immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry revealed differential changes in variant-specific interactions with known RAB3A regulatory and effector proteins.

biological.citation: RAB3 phosphorylation by pathogenic LRRK2 impairs trafficking of synaptic vesicle precursors (PMID: 38512027)
biological.summary: Hyperphosphorylation of RAB3A by pathogenic LRRK2-p.R1441H in iPSC-derived human neurons disrupts anterograde axonal transport of synaptic vesicle precursors, causing sequestration of synaptophysin and synaptobrevin-2 in the soma. RAB3A phosphorylation disrupts binding to the motor adaptor MADD, preventing formation of the RAB3A-MADD-KIF1A/1Bβ transport complex, and also disrupts interactions with RAB3GAP and RAB-GDI1.

biological.citation: Molecular and functional interactions of alpha-synuclein with Rab3a (PMID: 35809645)
biological.summary: Alpha-synuclein interacts with GTP-bound Rab3a via its C-terminus in a manner similar to its interaction with Rab8a, with the interaction strengthened on lipid membrane surfaces. Alpha-synuclein inhibits GTP hydrolysis by Rab3a, and this inhibition is more potent on membrane surfaces. Phosphorylation of alpha-synuclein at Ser129, associated with Parkinson's disease pathology, enhances its interaction with Rab3a and increases inhibition of Rab3a GTP hydrolysis.

biological.citation: Heterozygous RAB3A variants cause cerebellar ataxia by a partial loss-of-function mechanism (PMID: 40166812)
biological.summary: In a Drosophila Rab3 loss-of-function model, the two missense variants p.Arg83Trp and p.Tyr91Cys failed to rescue a synaptic phenotype, consistent with partial loss-of-function. Overexpression of Rab3 variants in a Drosophila wild-type background did not cause an obvious phenotype, making a dominant negative effect unlikely.

biological.citation: zDHHC9 Regulates Cardiomyocyte Rab3a Activity and Atrial Natriuretic Peptide Secretion Through Palmitoylation of Rab3gap1 (PMID: 37325411)
biological.summary: The Golgi S-acyltransferase zDHHC9 palmitoylates Rab3gap1, causing its spatial segregation from Rab3a, elevation of Rab3a-GTP levels, formation of Rab3a-positive peripheral vesicles, and impairment of exocytosis that limits atrial natriuretic peptide release in cardiomyocytes. This identifies a novel regulatory pathway linking palmitoylation to Rab3a GTP-loading state and cardiomyocyte exocytosis.

biological.citation: ASHG 2016 - Identification of interactions in the MADD PTPRN RAB3 complex with type 2 diabetes in multiple populations
biological.summary: Gene-gene interactions among MADD, PTPRN/PTPRN2, and RAB3A/RAB3C were identified in association with type 2 diabetes across eight independent multi-ethnic studies totaling 15,502 participants. MADD acts as a GDP/GTP exchange factor for RAB3A/RAB3C to provide energy for moving insulin-containing dense core secretory vesicles to the membrane for insulin release. Single-gene analyses did not find significant associations, highlighting the importance of the protein complex interaction.

biological.citation: Rab3A mediates vesicle delivery at photoreceptor ribbon synapses (PMID: 22593061)
biological.summary: Fluorescently labeled Rab3A binds to and dissociates from synaptic ribbons in tiger salamander photoreceptors in a GTP hydrolysis-dependent manner. A GTPase-deficient Rab3A mutant blocks synaptic release in an activity-dependent manner in paired recordings from photoreceptors and OFF-bipolar cells. These findings suggest Rab3A plays a crucial role in delivering vesicles to Ca²⁺-dependent release sites at ribbon synapses.

biological.citation: Rab3A interacts with spastin to regulate neurite outgrowth in hippocampal neurons (PMID: 36587525)
biological.summary: Rab3A physically interacts with spastin in rat brain lysates and co-localizes with spastin in cultured hippocampal neurons. Rab3A overexpression induces lysosomal and ubiquitin-mediated degradation of spastin, abolishing spastin-mediated microtubule severing. Overexpression of Rab3A inhibits neurite outgrowth while knockdown promotes it, with the inhibitory effect reversed by co-transfection of spastin.

biological.citation: Association of variants in the KIF1A gene with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (PMID: 36284339)
biological.summary: ALS-associated KIF1A variants in the C-terminal cargo-binding region preferentially enhanced binding of synaptic vesicle precursors containing RAB3A, VAMP2, and synaptophysin. Expression of disease-related KIF1A mutants in cultured mouse cortical neurons led to enhanced colocalization of RAB3A with the KIF1A motor, suggesting dysregulated RAB3A-containing vesicle transport in ALS pathogenesis.

biological.citation: Rab3a attenuates spinal cord injury by mediating vesicle release (PMID: 38253132)
biological.summary: Rab3a was significantly downregulated in a rat spinal cord injury (SCI) model, and Rab3a overexpression promoted SCI repair. Rab3a knockdown in neuronal cells inhibited secretion of neuronal cell-derived extracellular vesicles and promoted M1 macrophage polarization and neuronal apoptosis. STXBP1 was identified as a binding protein of Rab3a, and their interaction promoted neuronal cell-derived EV secretion; METTL2b was found to regulate Rab3a protein expression.
